question: What is the primary reason nurses change a bedbound patient's position regularly?

options.A: To help the patient eat faster during meal times
options.B: To prevent skin breakdown and maintain joint mobility
options.C: To make it easier to change the bed sheets daily
options.D: To ensure the doctor can examine the patient quickly

explanation: Regular movement relieves pressure on bony areas and keeps joints from stiffening during prolonged bed rest. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which patient group requires the most frequent and careful positioning by the nurse?

options.A: Clients with complete physical paralysis or heavy sedation
options.B: Clients waiting for minor outpatient diagnostic tests
options.C: Clients walking around the ward before morning discharge
options.D: Clients sitting comfortably in a chair reading a book

explanation: Individuals who cannot move on their own are at the highest risk for complications like pressure injuries and contractures. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h1)

question: What tool should a nurse use to fill gaps between the patient's body and the mattress?
explanation: Support devices like pillows distribute weight evenly and maintain natural body contours. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h2)

question: Why must a nurse lift a patient across the bed instead of dragging them?

options.A: Lifting is much faster for the nurse to complete alone
options.B: Dragging causes the mattress to lose its inner foam shape
options.C: Dragging creates too much static electricity on the bed sheets
options.D: Lifting prevents friction and shear damage to the skin layers

explanation: Friction and shear tear delicate superficial blood vessels and lead to rapid skin breakdown. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h2)

question: How is a client positioned during the supine posture?

options.A: Flat on their stomach with the head turned sideways
options.B: Lying on the left side with knees pulled up
options.C: Flat on their back with the face pointing upward
options.D: Sitting upright at a ninety degree bed angle

explanation: The supine position rests the entire dorsal surface of the body against the mattress. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h3)

question: A client in the prone position is lying on which part of their body?
explanation: The prone position places the client face down on their stomach area. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h3)

question: Which nursing procedure is most commonly performed with the patient in the Sims position?
explanation: The Sims position exposes the anal area and follows the natural curve of the lower intestine. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h4)

question: What distinguishes the Sims position from a standard lateral position?

options.A: The client's feet are elevated higher than the heart
options.B: The client leans further forward onto the chest and abdomen
options.C: The client lies flat on the back with legs wide apart
options.D: The head of the bed is raised to a full ninety degrees

explanation: Sims is a semi-prone posture where weight shifts forward onto the anterior chest and ilium. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is the typical bed elevation angle for a semi-Fowler's position?
explanation: Semi-Fowler's elevates the head moderately to aid breathing without placing too much pressure on the sacrum. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why is the high Fowler's position chosen for a patient experiencing severe shortness of breath?

options.A: It completely stops all blood flow from reaching the lower extremities
options.B: It drops the abdominal organs away from the diaphragm to expand lung capacity
options.C: It allows the patient to sleep deeply without waking up from coughing
options.D: It makes it easier for nurses to listen to bowel sounds in the stomach

explanation: Upright sitting uses gravity to pull abdominal contents down, giving the lungs maximum room to expand. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h5)

question: How is the bed adjusted during the Trendelenburg position?

options.A: Bed is completely flat and level
options.B: Knees are bent with head raised
options.C: Head is lower than the feet
options.D: Head is higher than the feet

explanation: Trendelenburg tilts the whole frame so the head rests lower than the lower extremities. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is a primary benefit of using the reverse Trendelenburg position?

options.A: Making rectal examinations easier for the clinician
options.B: Stopping severe bleeding in the lower extremities
options.C: Instantly increasing dangerously low blood pressure
options.D: Reducing acid reflux and promoting gastric emptying

explanation: Gravity helps keep stomach contents down in the lower GI tract when the upper body is tilted upward. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which surgical or exam position places the patient's feet in stirrups?
explanation: The lithotomy position uses stirrups to support the elevated legs during pelvic and perineal procedures. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h7)

question: What major complication can occur if a patient stays in the lithotomy position for too long?

options.A: Complete paralysis of the upper cervical spine
options.B: Rapid development of sacral pressure ulcers
options.C: Peroneal nerve damage from improper stirrup pressure
options.D: Sudden severe fluid overload in the lung alveoli

explanation: Pressure from stirrups against the lateral knee can damage the peroneal nerve and cause foot drop. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h7)

question: What is the standard frequency for turning an immobile client in bed?
explanation: Turning clients every two hours relieves sustained pressure on capillaries and prevents skin breakdown. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h8)

question: Why is a footboard used for a bedbound client?

options.A: To give the patient something to push against when standing
options.B: To stop the bottom bed sheets from getting wrinkled
options.C: To prevent foot drop by keeping feet in a neutral position
options.D: To keep the nursing call bell within easy reach

explanation: Footboards support the feet at a ninety-degree angle, stopping plantar flexion deformities. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h8)

question: What specific detail should be recorded after changing a client's position?

options.A: The exact weight of the pillows used for support
options.B: The exact time and the specific position used
options.C: The personal opinions of visiting family members
options.D: The brand name of the hospital bed mattress

explanation: Recording times and positions proves that turning schedules were maintained for skin protection. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h9)

question: What does a reddened skin area that fails to turn white when pressed indicate?

options.A: Normal healing from a previous minor scratch
options.B: A healthy increase in local blood circulation
options.C: An allergic reaction to the cotton bed sheet
options.D: Early tissue damage requiring immediate intervention

explanation: Non-blanching erythema means blood vessels have suffered deep ischemic damage, signaling an emerging pressure ulcer. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h9)
